name: eutl-installation-net-short

task.question: At the close of compliance year t-1's surrender cycle (30 April of year t), will a stationary EU ETS installation's verified emissions for year t exceed the free allocation it holds for year t (a net-short year), given its verified-emissions and free-allocation history through t-1, its already-published year-t allocation, its registry and its identifier?
task.prediction_time: 30 April of compliance year t, the surrender deadline that closes year t-1's compliance cycle: by then the installation's verified emissions for t-1 (reported by 31 March) and its surrendered allowances for t-1 are settled in the Union Registry, and its year-t free allocation is already fixed and published (the extract carries allocation rows through 2030, measured). Year t's verified emissions are reported by 31 March t+1 and are absent from the registry at the instant (measured: no numeric verified emissions for years after 2025 in the daily extract). The extract refreshes daily, so a monthly refresh of this task is honest.

feature_documentation: every shipped quantity is a Union Registry operators_yearly activity value (column semantics documented on the Union Registry Public Website data-download page, fetched by this build): VERIFIED_EMISSIONS and ALLOCATION are in tonnes CO2-equivalent (1 allowance = 1 tCO2e). ve_l1/alloc_l1 read year t-1; alloc_t reads the year-t free allocation fixed in advance by the phase-4 national implementation measures; margin/difference columns are derived in build.py's module docstring

measurements.unit: Union Registry country code (EU Member State, EEA-EFTA member or XI = Northern Ireland electricity)
measurements.frame: the installation's registry (country) identity; 32 registries measured on the 2026-10-22 snapshot
compliance year t, the year whose net-short status is predicted; the split time column

VERIFIED_EMISSIONS of year t-1, reported to the registry by 31 March of year t and settled at the instant; current-snapshot vintage (the registry can correct entries after the fact; only the current daily extract is available, so this is stated as current-vintage with the cutoff a documented assumption)
ALLOCATION of year t-1, as recorded in the registry at the instant

ALLOCATION of year t, fixed in advance by the phase-4 national implementation measures and published before the instant (measured: the extract carries allocation rows through 2030); one side of the label comparison but fully known at the instant and does not determine the label on its own
alloc_t - alloc_l1, the announced allocation change between the last settled year and the target year
ve_l1 - alloc_l1, the installation's net position at t-1; the persistence analogue the task must beat
ve_l1 - alloc_t, last verified emissions against the announced year-t allocation; the natural one-line solver rule
1 iff ve_l1 > alloc_l1, the status persistence rule (measured P(short t | short t-1) = 0.857, P(short t | long t-1) = 0.176 on eligible rows)
(t-1) minus the first year with numeric verified emissions in the extract; installations operating before 2005 have the age understated by the 2005 left edge - a documented left-truncation property
the installation identity across years; the event key because an installation's net-short status is autocorrelated year to year
unique per row; installations recur across split windows by construction of a panel - a declared property, not split leakage (the composite id is unique across all splits)
1 iff VERIFIED_EMISSIONS(t) > ALLOCATION(t); exact ties are 0 and counted (4,224 measured); both source values are excluded from the shipped columns

known_event.name: record sample rows and the phase-3 allocation cut
known_event.expected: (AT, installation 1, 2005) is net-long, (2007) is net-short, (2030) carries advance allocation with no emissions; the eligible-row net-short rate jumps from 2012 to 2013 by at least 0.25
known_event.source: Union Registry extract; candidate record sample_rows / discovery measurements, verified in-panel at discovery 2026-10-20/21

at_installation_1_2030.expected: advance allocation 30,485 with no verified emissions

phase3_allocation_cut_2013.expected: eligible-row net-short rate jumps by at least 0.25 (measured gap 0.331 at discovery)

prediction_instant.citation: Union Registry compliance calendar: verified emissions for year t-1 are reported by 31 March (Monitoring and Reporting Regulation (EU) 2018/2066 Art. 7) and allowances surrendered by 30 April (Directive 2003/87/EC Art. 12(3)) - 120 days after the t-1 period end. The instant is the close of year t-1's compliance cycle, when every shipped t-1 feature is settled in the registry and the year-t allocation is in force. The extract is an administrative record refreshed daily (SNAPSHOT_DATE 2026-10-22 measured; HTTP Last-Modified 2026-10-22 measured), so no separate statistical-release lag exists to observe; the statutory deadlines are the publisher's own calendar.

row_selection.basis: rows are (installation, year t) pairs whose label inputs VERIFIED_EMISSIONS(t) and ALLOCATION(t) are both numeric; a row without them is out of frame (counted per year in the frame mix, never silently dropped) - its own outcome is unobserved, and no other year's data affects membership. The latest period any feature reads is t-1 (ve_l1, alloc_l1) plus the pre-announced year-t allocation.

split_boundaries.excluded: 2005 (no t-1 history in the extract: 16709 installation-years insufficient_history, counted); 2026+ are live prediction years (6449 rows measured, scorable when verified emissions are reported)

id_columns_note: row_id is registry@installation@year, unique by construction; no identifier repeats inside a split or spans two. Installations recur across windows (a panel); that is a declared source property, and the composite row id keeps the identity checks meaningful.
positive_events_note: an event is one distinct installation carrying at least one net-short year in the window (the declared event key; the gate counts distinct 10-character prefixes of the key among positives, which merges long identifiers - both counts are recorded in summary.json). Positives also share year-level regime effects (the phase drift), documented as the per-year prevalence drift in the candidate record.
